title: kv-cache: improved eviction/defrag + async spillover paging to host memory
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: under real multi-tenant workloads the GPU KV cache suffers from fragmentation and out-of-memory spikes as long-lived prefixes intermingle with many short-lived contexts. This causes unpredictable evictions and latency regression when the runtime must fall back to model reloads or host-side token recomputation. This PR introduces a set of complementary changes to make KV cache memory management more robust: 1) a slab-based allocator and lightweight defragmentation pass to reduce fragmentation and improve allocation predictability; 2) an asynchronous spillover/paging mechanism that offloads cold KV pages to host memory (pinned GPU->host buffers) with background prefetching; 3) eviction heuristics that combine recency, token-span, and estimated re-use probability to reduce thrash; 4) new telemetry and guards exposed via config flags so operators can tune tradeoffs per workload. The description below summarizes design, implementation notes, tests, and rollout plan.
commits: feat(kv): introduce slab allocator and per-shard free lists
perf(kv): implement in-place defragmentation pass with pause/resume hooks
feat(kv): async spillover pipeline gpu->host pages with compression option
feat(kv): eviction scoring using recency + estimated reuse probability
ci(tests): add unit and integration tests for spillover and restore semantics
docs: add runtime config docs and observability dashboards
review_comments: Luca Romano: Please include a fall-back path if the host memory is saturated — how does the system degrade?
Maya Patel: Added host-memory pressure metrics and a reactive throttle (config:kv.spillover.max_host_bytes). If host is exhausted we accelerate eviction and surface a warning metric and log entry.
Erin Zhao: Can we get an upper bound on restore latency from host->GPU for worst-case page faults? Also add integration test for interleaved read/write during restore.

Maya Patel: Benchmarked restore latency in worst-case contiguous page read (see benchmarks/kv_cache/kv_eviction_benchmark.py) — p95 ~ 7.2ms on our internal p3-like instance when prefetch enabled; added integration test that stresses concurrent access during restore.
Samir Kapoor: How does defrag interact with continuous batching scheduling? Any amplification of latency spikes?

Maya Patel: Defrag runs in small incremental steps with yield points tied to the batching scheduler. If latency SLOs tighten, defrag will yield earlier; the scheduler exposes kv.defrag.max_step_ms and kv.defrag.yield_tokens to tune behavior. Added guard so defrag never runs during critical low-latency windows (config toggle and automatic suppression when active requests > threshold).
merge_commit_message: kv: robust KV cache memory management — slab allocator, defrag, async spillover, smarter eviction heuristics (squash)
release_notes: Improves KV cache stability under mixed workloads by reducing fragmentation and enabling async GPU->host spillover. Operators can tune kv.defrag.* and kv.spillover.* flags to balance latency and GPU memory utilization. Metrics: kv_defrag_runs_total, kv_spillover_pages, kv_restore_latency_ms. No user-facing API changes.
benchmarking_summary: Local benchmarks (benchmarks/kv_cache/kv_eviction_benchmark.py) show median latency unchanged, p95 token emit time reduced by ~12% for multi-tenant synthetic workload with 60% long-lived prefixes. Memory compaction yields 18-25% lower peak GPU memory usage depending on prefix distribution. Async spillover adds ~6-9% CPU overhead but prevents eviction storms and reduces model reload events in long tails.
ops_notes: Rollout plan: enable feature off by default. Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% via config toggle per cluster. Monitor kv_restore_latency_ms and kv_spillover_pages for signs of thrash. If restore latency > 50ms p95, enable kv.spillover.prefetch=false and increase kv.spillover.max_host_bytes.
documentation: Added docs/ops/kv_cache_tuning.md describing tuning knobs, recommended defaults for hosted vs dedicated deployments, and a troubleshooting section for common symptoms (eviction storms, high restore latency).
follow_up: ENG-4955: automatic adaptive thresholds for spillover based on workload telemetry; ENG-4982: optional compression codec selection per-tenant for spillover pages.
notes: This PR was prepared after the incident on 2025-01-29 where a multi-tenant mem-pressure event caused several Dedicated nodes to cascade into model reloads. The design focuses on predictable degradation and observability so SRE can set safe defaults per deployment tier.
